name: Dijon
label: R&R / Warner
lede: A military kid who cut his first records with a college friend in Maryland, spent years as the name in other people's credits, then made an album about his newborn son that Pitchfork ranked No. 2 of 2025.

eras.title: Two Maryland kids and a laptop
eras.text: Dijon Duenas grew up moving between bases, landed in Maryland, and made hazy R&B with a friend while finishing an English degree. The duo was the whole education: production, singing and how to stay out of the local scene's way.

years.cap: Abhi//Dijon, the Maryland duo Duenas started with Abhirath Raju.
years.src: The Fader: Dijon is imagining · SSENSE · The Washington Post · Wikipedia: Dijon Duenas
years.h: Abhi//Dijon: an English major and a producer put out EPs
years.p: Dijon Duenas graduated from the University of Maryland in 2014 with an English degree. He and high school friend Abhirath Raju released a compilation and two EPs of washed-out R&B between 2012 and 2016.
years.xp:
The Fader reported in 2018 that Duenas, a military kid shuttled between the U.S. and Germany, made his first beats on a four-track and FL Studio and only got serious about music in his last year at Maryland. SSENSE reports he first worked in Baltimore's DIY and punk circles before the R&B duo.

Duenas later told The Washington Post that Maryland was the place he lived longest, but that he always felt some distance from the music scene there. Wikipedia lists the releases as the self-titled EP (2014), Stay Up (2015) and Montana (2016).

years.src: The Fader: Dijon is imagining · Wikipedia: Dijon Duenas · Dazed
years.h: Duenas and Raju move to Los Angeles and split up quietly
years.p: After relocating in summer 2016, the duo dissolved without a fight and Duenas started over alone. As Abhi//Dijon they had also been credited on Nao's "Adore You" that year.
years.xp: Duenas told The Fader that in Los Angeles the switch to solo work "just happened organically and naturally." Wikipedia says the two disbanded amicably. Dazed lists the Nao credit as the first of several places his work was hiding in other people's records.

eras.title: The guy in the background of your favorite record
eras.text: Solo, but mostly heard through other people: backing vocals for a boy band collective, synths on a pandemic pop record, two EPs that few outside Los Angeles noticed yet.

years.h: Solo debut "Stranger" and backing vocals on Brockhampton's Saturation II
years.p: Duenas released his first solo single, "Stranger", the same year he sang backing vocals on [[Brockhampton|3ac96b4c-4f42-48c8-b793-84dbf54d7ac6]]'s Saturation II, including the song "Summer".
years.xp: The Brockhampton link ran deep: Duenas returned for songwriting and additional vocals on "1998 Truman" in 2018, and i-D's 2021 profile of him ran with photographs by the group's Kevin Abstract. Dazed counts "Summer" as one of the first spots where listeners heard him without knowing it.

years.h: Co-produces [[Charli XCX|260b6184-8828-48eb-945c-bc4cb6fc34ca]]'s "Pink Diamond" from her quarantine album
years.p: Working alongside [[A. G. Cook|b12ef43e-72ad-43d0-b216-a8cd32f78852]], Duenas is credited on production, songwriting, synthesizer and drum programming for the How I'm Feeling Now track.
years.xp: That same month Duenas put out his own EP, How Do You Feel About Getting Married?, on Dark Green, R&R and Warner, following Sci Fi 1 (March 1, 2019). He told NME the 2020 EP was where he stopped insisting on doing everything alone, because "friends came in and made it sound better."

eras.title: The guest-room record
eras.text: Absolutely arrives with a co-producer who becomes his closest ally, a short film, a talk-show slot and a spot on Barack Obama's summer playlist. For a record made in a house, it travels far.

q: The process was very simple; Mike played drums, I played a weird backup thing.
years.src: Wikipedia: Absolutely · NME · i-D · The Fader: Dijon on spontaneity · SSENSE
years.p: Duenas and Michael Gordon (Mk.gee) co-produced the debut album at Duenas's Los Angeles home and in upstate New York. Pitchfork scored it 7.2, The Fader ranked it No. 3 of 2021.
years.xp:
"Many Times" led on September 17, 2021, then "Rodeo Clown" on October 22. Duenas told NME the first single came together simply: "Mike played drums, I played a weird backup thing." i-D reported the crew used a single fixed microphone to catch the whole room, laughter and TV static included, and let first-time songwriter Noah Le Gros sing lead on "Noah's Highlight Reel."

A short film companion followed December 22, 2021. In summer 2022 Barack Obama put "Many Times" on his playlist, per Wikipedia.

years.src: Wikipedia: Dijon Duenas · Wikipedia: Absolutely · The Washington Post
yt: Big Mike's on The Tonight Show
years.h: "Big Mike's" on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon
years.p: Duenas's TV debut brought the messy room sound of the album into a network studio.
years.xp: That spring he opened two Bon Iver shows, in Mesa, Arizona and Austin, Texas, with a live band of Jack Karaszewski, Henry Kwapis, Mk.gee and Ryan Richter. He told The Washington Post: "we get pretty bored just trying to tell the same story." He then headlined his own North American tour that year.

eras.title: Everybody's secret co-writer, then his own record
eras.text: Between albums Duenas becomes the person other artists call. Then he finishes Baby, and the industry's part-time credit becomes the year's best-reviewed R&B record.

years.h: Writes and produces on Mk.gee's Two Star & the Dream Police
years.p: Duenas is credited as writer and producer on the record that made Mk.gee a critical name, released on R&R.
years.xp: Dazed's rundown of Duenas's hidden credits also lists production on Matt Champion's "Slow Motion" featuring Jennie, and vocals on "Aphid" from Champion's Mika's Laundry, both from 2024.

years.src: Wikipedia: Dijon Duenas · Dazed · Stereogum: Dijon Sings
years.p: Duenas is credited on four tracks. "Daisies", which he made with Mk.gee, reached No. 2 on the Hot 100.
years.xp: Wikipedia says Duenas also performs on "Devotion" and produced and co-wrote "Yukon", which reached No. 17. Stereogum reports he played "Yukon" live for the first time in Portland on November 1, 2025, and that Bieber had already shown up at one of his San Diego dates.

years.src: Exclaim! · Stereogum: Stream Dijon's Emotive · Wikipedia: Baby
years.h: Baby's release date comes with a legal disclaimer
years.p: That was the caption on the countdown clock Duenas posted a week ahead, with no singles released.
years.xp: Exclaim! reported the clock ran to midnight on August 14, with the album due the next day. Stereogum notes the album arrived without advance singles. The samples cleared; the album came out August 15.

years.src: Album of the Year · Wikipedia: Baby · Wikipedia: Dijon Duenas · The Fader: Review · Stereogum: Stream Dijon's Emotive · Dazed
years.h: Baby: fatherhood, samples and a kitchen sink
years.p: Pitchfork gave it 9.0 and ranked it No. 2 of 2025. Andrew Sarlo produced most of the 37 minutes, dedicated to his wife Joanie del Santo and their son.
years.xp:
Album of the Year's critic score list has Pitchfork at 90 and Paste at 100; Metacritic showed a 94 from seven reviews and Rolling Stone gave it 4.5 stars, per Wikipedia. Pitchfork's year-end list put it behind only Los Thuthanaka. Wikipedia lists Rolling Stone No. 4, Paste No. 5 and The Fader No. 13 on their year-end lists. Pitchfork is not fetchable from here, so the score is from Wikipedia and Album of the Year.

Beyond Sarlo and Mk.gee, credits include BJ Burton, Tommy King, Tobias Jesso Jr., Pino Palladino on bass and Justin Vernon on "Higher!", which also has Jenn Wasner of Baltimore's Wye Oak on bass. Vernon's Bon Iver had featured Duenas on "Day One" from Sable, Fable that April. The Fader described it as made at home, in isolation, with his family. Dazed says the title comes from the son born in 2023.

years.h: Acting debut in Paul Thomas Anderson's One Battle After Another
years.p: Duenas appears in Paul Thomas Anderson's film alongside Leonardo DiCaprio, Teyana Taylor and Alana Haim.
years.xp: Dazed and Primetimer both flagged the role as his first screen work. Wikipedia lists the film's release in September 2025.

years.src: The Baltimore Banner · Wikipedia: Grammy Award
years.h: Two Grammy nominations, neither for his own album
years.p: Producer of the Year, Non-Classical, and Album of the Year for Swag.
years.xp: The Baltimore Banner reported both nominations. At the February 2026 ceremony Cirkut won the producer award, per Wikipedia.

years.cap: Dijon on Saturday Night Live, hosted by Melissa McCarthy.
years.src: The Baltimore Banner · Rolling Stone · Primetimer
years.p: Melissa McCarthy hosted; Duenas played two songs from Baby the night after a sold-out Fillmore Silver Spring show near his old Maryland stomping grounds.
years.xp: The Baltimore Banner tied the appearance to his Ellicott City roots: he attended Centennial High School before Maryland. The Fillmore Silver Spring show on December 5 was sold out.

eras.title: "Couchella"
eras.text: The Baby cycle ends on a desert stage, with a band assembled like a jam session and filmed like a concert movie.

years.cap: Dijon at Coachella, Empire Polo Club, Indio.
years.h: Coachella debut: eight musicians in a horseshoe
years.p: Paste compared the set to Stop Making Sense. Mk.gee played distorted guitar and Jack Karaszewski mixed live.
years.xp: Paste reports the walkout used a pitched-up Family Guy theme and the band built each song from scratch, with cameras on stage. The stream was up only until 4 p.m. on April 11. Setlist.fm lists a second weekend set on April 17.
